title: Hymn 2, sound: chhia ghar
hookLine: chhia ghar chhia gur chhia updes (Asa M1, ang 12)

lines: A LINE BUILT LIKE A DRUMBEAT.
cards: Some lines are built like a drumbeat. You hear the pattern before you understand a word. Chhia ghar.
Chhia gur. Chhia updes. Three beats, the same little word starting each one.
Even with no Punjabi at all, you can tell something is being counted. It's Sohila's second hymn, Guru Nanak's again, this time in Raag Asa, still on Ang 12.
After yesterday's gentle wedding, this one opens short and sharp, like someone tapping a table three times.

teach.b: The first line: chhia ghar chhia gur chhia updes. Chhia means six. Ghar you met two days ago: a house.
Here it means a house of thought, a school. Gur is a teacher. Updes is a teaching, instruction.
So: six schools, six teachers, six teachings. Then the second line answers the drumbeat: gur gur eko ves anek.

teach.h: GUR GUR EKO: ONE GURU OF GURUS.
teach.b: The Guru of those gurus is One; the forms are many. Eko means one, like the Ik of Ik Onkar. Ves is a form, a dress, a guise.
Anek means many. In two lines Guru Nanak counts six, and lands on one. Then the refrain.
In paraphrase: O Baba, the house in which the Creator's praise is sung, hold on to that house; in it lies your greatness. Hear the echo?
Yesterday's hymn began with the house where praise is sung, and today's refrain comes back to the same house.
In Sohila the hymns talk to each other, and the word ghar runs through both like a thread. Tomorrow, who the six schools were. Today, just keep the shape: six, six, six, and then one.
A count that ends in unity.

how: This is the second of the five hymns Sikhs recite each night in Kirtan Sohila; in gurdwaras it is recited when the Guru Granth Sahib is put to rest for the night.

o: a holy house where a teacher lives
a teaching, instruction from a teacher
the number six, counted out in a hymn

games.q: the second hymn, word by word — tap the pairs.

s: Sohila's second hymn is by Guru Arjan
it's by Guru Nanak, in Raag Asa, on Ang 12.
eko in the second line means one, like Ik in Ik Onkar
the word ghar links the first two hymns of Sohila
both come back to the house where the Creator's praise is sung.

games.q: the hymn has just counted six schools, six teachers, six teachings. what does the next line say?
o: that one of the six is right.
that the Guru of the gurus is One, in many forms.
that all six should be forgotten.
games.why: gur gur eko ves anek: the count of six ends in one Guru wearing many forms.

practice: Say the line slowly, tapping a finger on each beat: chhia ghar, chhia gur, chhia updes. Then say the answer, gur gur eko ves anek, and let your hand rest flat on that one.
Sit and feel the difference between counting and resting; if you pray, say Waheguru as you breathe out.

wordCard.voice: Updes, a teaching: Sohila's second hymn, by Guru Nanak in Raag Asa, six schools, six teachers, six teachings, and one Guru of gurus in many forms.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: chhia, six; the word that beats three times in the hymn's first line.

carryVoice: Your line: chhia ghar. Six houses, and one Guru behind them. Day four hundred twenty-four.
